attrs.evidence: spec_release.mjs v0.3.0 releaseId() = srel-H(RELEASE_TYPE | canonicalWire(release_core)); releases/<spec_release_id>.json WRITTEN on issuance, never overwritten with differing bytes, and required on every verification run to byte-match SPEC-RELEASE.json; a mechanical two-sided identity audit perturbs all 16 core leaves (each MUST move srel) and 3 declared non-core fields (each MUST NOT), where a one-way sweep would have passed over the replacer defect; the blind-implementation contract moved out of spec_digest into experiment_digest. Measured: changing one hidden holdout entry at identical revision labels moves spec_release_id and restoring it returns the identity. Gate `gov-nest`; grid boolean spec-release-bound.
attrs.statement: A RELEASE HAS ONE IDENTITY THAT BINDS EVERY COMMITMENT IT MAKES. Four component digests standing side by side with nothing over them do not identify a release: measured, changing one hidden holdout file and reissuing at the same revision numbers produced a second, different experiment still advertised as `spec revision 1 (a11e066a...)`, because the spec digest and corpus digest were unchanged. `spec_release_id = srel-H(release-core)` binds release type, protocol identifiers, spec revision and digest, experiment revision and digest, corpus revision and digest, the pinned upstream dependency repository, commit and digest, and the holdout commitment -- excluding only itself and explicitly non-authoritative prose. REVISION NUMBERS ARE LABELS AND DIGESTS ARE IDENTITIES; a conformance report cites the identity. AND PROCEDURE IS NOT PROTOCOL: a document that says of itself that it is procedural must not be inside the digest that says the wire protocol changed, so experiment revision and digest are a separate plane that the release identity also binds. Releases are immutable objects written under their own identity, with the conventional filename a pointer rather than the only copy -- and P4.6 made that MEASURED after a round in which it was aspirational: the evidence below named an archive that did not exist, while issuance overwrote one file and left no copy of the superseded release anywhere. AND THE IDENTITY MUST BIND WHAT THE INVARIANT SAYS IT BINDS: the preimage was built by a JSON.stringify replacer ARRAY, which is an allowlist applied RECURSIVELY, so the nested protocol map serialised as {} and renaming all three protocols left spec_release_id byte-identical. The preimage is canonicalWire(release_core) now, under the same RFC 8785 encoder the wire protocol uses and gates against six upstream vectors as octets.
